description: Versioned machine-readable contract for the Harvest management API. Update this file and CHANGELOG.md whenever a route is added, removed, renamed, or its request/response shape changes.

breaking_changes: Changing the type of a response field
Renaming a route (path or method change)
Changing a query parameter from optional to required
Adding a new mutating route without classifying it in this contract
non_breaking_changes: Adding a new optional response field
Adding a new optional query parameter
Adding a new optional request body field
Narrowing an existing error response to be more specific

auth_note: Route authorization posture is classified in issue #174. This contract records the route surface and category; auth enforcement is separate.
audit_note: Mutating routes (read_only: false) are covered by the audit trail (issue #158). The audit endpoint itself is read-only.

routes.description: List workflow executions with optional filters. Supports keyset cursor pagination (issue #498).

params.name: search_attr
params.description: Search attribute filter in key:value form (exact-match string equality). May be repeated.

params.name: search_attr_filter
params.description: Typed comparison/set predicate over search attributes in key:op:value form, op in {eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, exists} (issue #506). Repeatable; ANDed. Numeric values compare numerically, booleans as booleans, else strings. Comparison ops require a numeric value. Malformed predicates and nested .-paths return 400. Backed by the existing idx_harvest_we_search GIN index (no migration).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of results to return (legacy; use page_size for paginated access).

params.name: page_size
params.description: Number of results per page (1–200). Activates the paginated response envelope {workflows, next_cursor}.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Opaque keyset pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor field.

params.name: order
params.description: Sort direction: 'asc' (oldest first) or 'desc' (newest first, default). Activates the paginated response envelope.

params.name: started_after
params.description: Filter to executions whose started_at is after this RFC 3339 timestamp (e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z).

params.name: started_before
params.description: Filter to executions whose started_at is before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

params.name: exec_id_prefix
params.description: Case-insensitive prefix match on the execution UUID string.

params.name: sla_breached
params.description: When 'true', return only executions whose soft SLA has been breached (issue #487).

params.name: nd_blocked
params.description: When 'true', return only RUNNING executions currently blocked on replay non-determinism (issue #603). Each row carries nd_blocked_at / nd_block_reason / nd_block_count plus the structured divergence diagnostic (failure_cause, expected, actual, event_index, workflow_type, build_id) in search_attrs.

params.name: legal_hold
params.description: When 'true', return only executions currently under an active legal hold (issue #747): legal_hold_set_at IS NOT NULL AND (legal_hold_until IS NULL OR legal_hold_until > now).

success_response.description: Without pagination params: bare JSON array of execution objects (backward compatible). With cursor/page_size/order: JSON object {"workflows": [...], "next_cursor": <string|null>}.

error_responses.description: Invalid filter value, bad RFC 3339 timestamp, or unknown order direction.

routes.description: Grouped execution-count fleet snapshot (issue #544): counts harvest_workflow_executions rows grouped by state and/or workflow_name across all shards, computed with a per-shard SQL GROUP BY and summed in-process. Eventually-consistent point-in-time snapshot; no replay or ordering guarantee under concurrent writes. An unreachable shard is named in unavailable_shards rather than failing the call wholesale.

params.name: group_by
params.description: Comma-separated grouping dimensions: state, workflow_name, or state,workflow_name. Defaults to state.

params.name: workflow_name
params.description: Filter by registered workflow name (applied before grouping).

params.name: state
params.description: Comma-separated or repeated execution states (e.g. RUNNING,FAILED) to include (applied before grouping).

params.name: started_after
params.description: Filter to executions whose started_at is on or after this RFC 3339 timestamp.

params.name: started_before
params.description: Filter to executions whose started_at is on or before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

params.name: limit_groups
params.description: Cap on returned (state, workflow_name) groups (default 50, max 500); long tail rolls into a single group with other:true.

error_responses.description: Invalid parameter value (unknown group_by dimension, unknown state, malformed timestamp, or out-of-range limit_groups).

routes.description: List tiered/summary-retention execution summaries (issue #752): compact, queryable rows the retention janitor demotes a hard-deleted terminal execution into instead of losing it entirely. Admin-guarded (summaries may carry retained/redacted payloads). Cross-shard fan-out with the same keyset-cursor pagination contract as GET /workflows (issue #498), ordered by (completed_at DESC, execution_id DESC). Each item carries summarized:true and history_available:false so it is unambiguously distinguishable from a live execution. An unreachable shard fails the call (matching GET /workflows).

params.name: workflow_name
params.description: Filter by registered workflow name (exact match).

params.name: state
params.description: Comma-separated or repeated terminal states (e.g. COMPLETED,FAILED).

params.name: completed_after
params.description: Filter to summaries whose completed_at is on or after this RFC 3339 timestamp.

params.name: completed_before
params.description: Filter to summaries whose completed_at is on or before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

params.name: search_attr
params.description: Search-attribute containment filter in key:value form (JSONB @> exact-match). May be repeated; ANDed.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 50, max 500). page_size is accepted as an alias.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Opaque keyset pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor field.

params.name: order
params.description: Sort direction: 'desc' (default, newest-first) or 'asc'. Any other value returns 400. Threaded through both the ordering and the keyset cursor comparison, matching GET /workflows (issue #498).

success_response.description: JSON object {"summaries": [...], "next_cursor": <string|null>}. Each summary carries execution_id, workflow_name, workflow_id, state, started_at, completed_at, duration_ms, shard_id, search_attrs, result, error, summarized_at, plus summarized:true and history_available:false.

error_responses.description: Invalid parameter value (unknown state, malformed timestamp, malformed search_attr, malformed cursor, or non-numeric limit).

error_responses.description: Invalid execution ID or wait duration.

params.name: status

routes.description: Show the current wait state of a running workflow (what it is blocked on).

success_response.notes: Each entry in pending_activities and pending_local_activities carries an optional nested last_failure object (issue #773) — {error_type, error, attempt, non_retryable, failed_at?, details?} — omitted entirely when the activity has never failed, so healthy-run responses stay byte-identical to pre-#773 builds. It answers "why is this activity retrying?" alongside the next_retry_at countdown without a second round-trip. Availability of the fields differs by activity kind because retryable failures are not event-sourced (an AC2-vs-AC5 reconciliation; #773 adds no migration): for a backing-off REGULAR (task-queue) activity — the primary case — last_failure is sourced from the harvest_task_queue.error column that queue::requeue_for_retry sets on each retryable failure (no ActivityFailed event is appended), so error and attempt are present, error_type defaults to "Error", non_retryable is false, and failed_at/details are omitted (the task row has no failure timestamp or structured detail); for LOCAL activities (and any event-sourced failure) last_failure is sourced from the most recent LocalActivityFailed event and includes failed_at (the event timestamp), with error_type "Error", non_retryable false, and no details. When read-path payload decoding (issue #608) is active for the request, last_failure.error is tolerantly decoded like every other payload field.

routes.description: Reconstruct a single execution's timeline (per-step durations, busy-vs-wait split, slowest step) purely from recorded history; no new events are appended and no state is recomputed. Surfaces only durations, names, ids, and outcomes — never any input/output/payload/error/value field — so read-path payload decoding (issue #608) is a no-op and is skipped. Classic DAG runs are not on the execution path and return 404; unified DAG runs lower onto the standard execution path and return 200 like any workflow execution. The wait_ms/exec_ms split is present ONLY for regular activity steps that recorded a claim/start timestamp; it is null for child_workflow, local_activity, external activities (issue #92 — these render as activity steps with no split), timer, signal_wait, side_effect, and for activities with no recorded start. total_ms is always present. Rollup attribution: a started activity's queue-wait split goes to rollup.wait_ms and its exec split to rollup.busy_ms; a regular activity (one reporting an attempt) with a null split never started (pending or a schedule-to-start timeout) so its whole total_ms is queue-wait and goes to rollup.wait_ms; external activities, child_workflow, local_activity, and side_effect totals go to rollup.busy_ms; timer and signal_wait totals go to rollup.wait_ms. For a retried activity, wait_ms spans all prior attempts' execution and backoff, not only queue wait — treat it as an upper bound on queue wait. Known limitation: the full event history is loaded with no LIMIT (bounded by workflow continue-as-new discipline, the ≤500-event target), so a run with a very large history makes this read proportionally expensive.

error_responses.description: Execution not found (including a classic DAG run, which is not on the execution path).

routes.idempotency: Fully idempotent; read-only.

routes.description: Reconstruct the ordered continue-as-new run chain that {id} belongs to, resolvable from ANY member (origin, a middle run, or the live/final tail). A workflow that calls continue_as_new forks forward into a fresh exec_id sharing its workflow_id and shard; over a long-lived self-continuing workflow this produces a chain of executions, and this endpoint returns all of them oldest-first as a flat list so one logical run's whole history is discoverable from a single member. The chain lives entirely on one shard (a successor inherits the predecessor's shard), so this is one shard-local gather, never a cross-shard fan-out. No new events are appended and no state is recomputed. Post-feature (issue #701) rows carry back-link columns (continued_from_exec_id, first_exec_id) so the chain resolves in one indexed query; legacy rows written before the feature carry no back-links and are gathered best-effort by forward-walking WorkflowContinuedAsNew events (bounded), with head_unknown=true when the true origin cannot be proven from the available rows. head_unknown=false for a fully post-feature chain and for a standalone never-continued run (runs has exactly one entry). Each run reports exec_id, run_id, sequence (zero-based chain ordinal), state, started_at, completed_at, outcome (collapsed terminal label), and continued_to_exec_id (the next ordered run's exec_id; null for the tail). continued_to_exec_id is derived purely from ordering so it stays correct for legacy chains that never stored a forward index. Documented graceful degradation: in a mixed chain (legacy prefix then post-feature suffix) resolved from a post-feature member, the boundary run is reported as the confirmed head and its truly-first legacy predecessors are unreachable.

params.name: id
params.description: Execution UUID of any member of the chain.

error_responses.description: Execution not found (including a classic DAG run, which is not on the execution path).

routes.idempotency: Fully idempotent; read-only.

fields.name: reuse_policy
fields.description: Duplicate-id policy: allow_duplicate, reject_duplicate, allow_duplicate_failed_only, or terminate_if_running.

fields.name: start_at
fields.description: Target ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp to start the workflow.

fields.name: delay
fields.description: Delay duration before starting the workflow (e.g. "10s", "5m").

fields.name: batch_key
fields.description: Optional event batching group key. Fold trigger starts into a single run inputting a JSON array of all payloads.

fields.name: batch_max_size
fields.description: Maximum batch size to trigger immediate flush.

fields.name: batch_max_wait
fields.description: Maximum wait duration from first trigger before flushing the batch (e.g. "30s", "5m").

fields.name: completion_callbacks
fields.description: Per-execution completion-callback targets (issue #605): a JSON array of {url, filter} objects. Each target's URL is validated against the operator-configured SSRF host allowlist before admission; a non-allowlisted target rejects the start with 422.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Request-scoped idempotency key (issue #808). Two starts carrying the same key within the retention window (default 24h) converge on exactly one execution: the first creates it, the second returns the same execution_id as a no-op (200, no second WorkflowStarted, no second task). Dedup scope is (workflow_name, idempotency_key), independent of workflow_id, and short-circuits the reuse_policy matrix. A committed keyed replay short-circuits to the 200 no-op before fresh-start-only validations (input-schema #373, completion-callback SSRF #605, delay/start_at) and before the admission gate #377, returning the original execution regardless of the retry's body; a genuinely fresh keyed start (no live claim) still runs every validation and the gate. The `Idempotency-Key` request header takes precedence over this body field; a present-but-empty key returns 400. Mutually exclusive with a throttle/debounce/batch policy (400 if combined). Shard routing: a keyed start with an OMITTED (auto-generated) workflow_id routes by the key so same-key retries co-locate and dedup; a keyed start with an EXPLICIT workflow_id routes by workflow_id (preserving the reuse_policy matrix and the shard-local (workflow_name, workflow_id) uniqueness invariant). For dedup to converge across a delivery's retries, be consistent about supplying vs. omitting workflow_id.

success_response.note: Returns 200 when an existing execution is returned via reuse_policy instead of creating a new one. Returns 200 with {..., started_fresh: false, deduplicated: true} when an idempotency_key (issue #808) matched an earlier same-key start (no new execution created); a fresh idempotency_key start returns 201 with {..., started_fresh: true, deduplicated: false}. The `Idempotency-Key` header may supply the key out-of-band instead of the body field. Returns 202 Accepted with {debounced, workflow_name, workflow_id, debounce_key, fire_at, pending_count} (and no execution_id) when the workflow declares a debounce policy whose key resolves (issue #499). Returns 202 Accepted with {batched, flushed, workflow_name, workflow_id, batch_key, fire_at, pending_count, max_size} when the workflow declares a batch policy.

error_responses.description: Invalid request body or workflow name. Also returned when start_at/delay is combined with a debounce policy, when input exceeds the workflow input cap, when idempotency_key is empty, or when idempotency_key is combined with a throttle/debounce/batch policy (issue #808).
Duplicate workflow_id with conflicting reuse policy.

Admission blocked by an active gate (including the debounce-key shard gate for debounced starts). A retry of an already-successful idempotency_key start (issue #808) bypasses the gate and returns the existing execution as a 200 no-op instead, since it is not fresh admission; a genuinely fresh keyed start is still gated.

routes.description: Cancel a running workflow execution.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: cancelling an already-cancelled or terminal execution is a no-op.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Human-readable cancellation reason recorded in audit log.

error_responses.description: Execution is already in a terminal state.

routes.description: Force-terminate a single workflow execution. The forceful sibling of cancel: seals a live run in the TERMINATED state unilaterally (no workflow-body cooperation required), fails outstanding task-queue rows, and runs the parent-close cascade. Result-awaiting callers observe a terminal failure carrying the supplied reason, distinguishable from a normal FAILED. Interrupting an already-executing hot workflow task is the domain of the workflow-task timeout (#494), not terminate.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: terminating an already-terminal execution (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT/TERMINATED/CONTINUED_AS_NEW) is a non-mutating no-op that appends no second terminal transition and returns newly_terminated=false.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Human-readable termination reason recorded on the execution and in the audit log.

routes.description: Pause a running workflow execution. While paused the executor dispatches no new commands; in-flight activities run to completion. PAUSED is a non-terminal active state.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: pausing an already-paused execution is a no-op (newly_paused=false).

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Human-readable pause reason (max 500 chars) recorded on the execution row (pause_reason) and the WorkflowExecutionPaused history event.

error_responses.description: Pause reason exceeds the length cap.
Execution is in a terminal state and cannot be paused.

routes.description: Resume a paused workflow execution, re-arming command dispatch and waking the parked task. Resuming a non-paused (running or terminal) execution is a success no-op reporting newly_resumed=false.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: resuming a non-paused execution is a 200 no-op (newly_resumed=false); nothing is mutated.

routes.description: Tombstone all payload-bearing fields (input, output, payload, details, value, last_completion_result) in every event row, the execution row, and signal rows for a terminal workflow execution. Cascades to terminal child executions on the same shard. Requires the execution to be in a terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT, CONTINUED_AS_NEW, or TERMINATED).
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: re-running on an already-erased execution returns fields_tombstoned=0, no error.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Human-readable erasure reason (e.g. GDPR Art. 17 request ID), recorded in audit log.

error_responses.description: Execution is not in a terminal state, or is under an active legal hold (issue #747) — erasure is rejected until the hold is released or expires.

routes.description: Place (or refresh) a per-execution legal hold (issue #747). An active hold exempts the execution's event history from retention deletion (issue #737) and from PII erasure (issue #495) until the hold is released or auto-expires. Additive nullable columns only; shard-local (routed via the execution UUID). Admin-only, audited under legal_hold.set.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: if an active hold already exists, its provenance is left unchanged and newly_held=false is returned (no write). A previously-set-but-expired hold is refreshed.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Operator-supplied justification for the hold (e.g. litigation hold case number), recorded in legal_hold_reason and the audit log. Truncated to 500 characters.

fields.name: hold_until
fields.description: Optional RFC3339 auto-expiry. Omit for an indefinite hold released only by an explicit release call.

error_responses.description: Malformed execution id or hold_until (not RFC3339).

routes.description: Release a per-execution legal hold (issue #747): NULLs all four legal_hold_* columns so the execution becomes eligible for retention and PII erasure again. Admin-only, audited under legal_hold.release.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: releasing an execution with no hold set returns released=false (200 no-op).

routes.description: Force a backing-off activity to retry immediately by advancing its scheduled_at to NOW() and waking an idle worker via pg_notify. Only PENDING tasks (including those waiting out exponential backoff) can be advanced. Local activities run inline and have no task-queue row — this endpoint does not apply to them.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: calling on an already-eligible task (scheduled_at <= now) returns advanced=false and performs no update. Calling twice after advancing also returns advanced=false on the second call.

params.name: activity_exec_id
params.description: Activity execution ID (the task-queue row PK, surfaced as activity_exec_id in GET /workflows/{id}/stack).

field_notes.advanced: true when scheduled_at was moved to immediate eligibility; false otherwise. Note: advanced=true means scheduled_at was updated, not that the task will be dispatched immediately — per-queue rate-limit buckets and concurrency caps in claim_task can still defer actual dispatch.
field_notes.already_eligible: Only meaningful when advanced=false. true=task was already claimable (idempotent no-op). false=a concurrent worker claimed the task between the SELECT and UPDATE (task is now RUNNING).
field_notes.next_retry_at: The backdated scheduled_at written to the task when advanced=true (immediately claimable). null when advanced=false.

error_responses.description: Execution or activity task not found, including task belonging to a different workflow, or activity_exec_id is not a valid UUID. Note: external-handoff activity IDs are a different id-space from task-queue PKs; passing one will return 404.
Task is not in PENDING state (e.g. currently RUNNING or already terminal).

routes.description: Force-fail exactly one hung in-flight (RUNNING) activity task. Appends ActivityFailed with the distinct error_type 'OperatorForceFailed' through the existing recording path (no new event variant), marks the task row FAILED with the typed failure envelope, and wakes the parked workflow task so the owning workflow advances to its own failure/compensation path -- it is NOT terminated. Remaining retry attempts are skipped regardless of retry policy (the forced failure is non-retryable by construction), and a late result from the worker still running the activity is ignored (no double-apply). Only RUNNING activity tasks of a non-terminal execution are force-failable. Note: if the owning workflow has a workflow-level retry policy (issue #523) and propagates this error to workflow failure, the run is retried fresh and the activity re-dispatched -- use cancel/terminate instead if the goal is to stop the run. Local activities run inline and have no task-queue row -- this endpoint does not apply to them (404).
routes.idempotency: Idempotent: re-issuing the call on an already-forced task (FAILED with the OperatorForceFailed envelope) is a no-op success returning forced=false, already_forced=true, with zero writes and no second terminal event. Idempotency wins over the terminal-execution guard: a retry issued after the woken workflow has consumed the forced failure and sealed its own run (the expected aftermath of a successful force-fail) still returns the no-op success rather than the terminal 409.

params.name: activity_exec_id
params.description: Activity execution ID (the task-queue row PK, surfaced as activity_exec_id in GET /workflows/{id}/stack).
